### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/service-print`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **128** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-print/LICENSE`, `packages/services/service-print/README.md`, `packages/services/service-print/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**61** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-print/LICENSE`, `packages/services/service-print/README.md`, `packages/services/service-print/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 37 pages)`
- **32** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `004ff06ee7fbd9d3d625a8474749bfba56342475` — the merge of head `5a16f29db960f6d14e058af2b926d959c8992a7e` into base `161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 004ff06ee7fbd9d3d625a8474749bfba56342475 && git checkout 004ff06ee7fbd9d3d625a8474749bfba56342475
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569 5a16f29db960f6d14e058af2b926d959c8992a7e && git checkout -B drift-repro 161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569 && git merge --no-ff 5a16f29db960f6d14e058af2b926d959c8992a7e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 161aee10478de783f37320d4f665153488571569` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · REWORK (patch round 1) · `domain:services` seat 2 · `session_018VqJPGA1NDNSCZsnecsChP` · 2026-10-16T04:34Z

Reviewed against GitHub at head `4aa215ac5c` and against the report `6208035645` on #22269. The build is sound where measured: a real render on both placements with a normal sign-in session, the refusal chain before any mint or launch, revoke in `finally`, the CJK pin ablated through a Latin-only fontconfig, and the archive committed. It cannot land yet, for two reasons the report itself names, plus the bind.

**Blocking, with the seat's answers:**
1. **The mint does not boot the console** (report `open_questions[0]`). This is now #23813, an in-scope sub-issue of #22269 in this lane, claimed (`6208138185`) and dispatched. This PR binds `mintPrincipalSession` after #23813 lands. Then: merge `origin/main`, bind through `src/principal-session.ts`, and run the real render with a MINTED session on both placements. That run is the card's acceptance; the sign-in-session run is not.
2. **The archive must attach under the caller** (report Q3). Ruling OQ7 A (`6059363716`) reads "pending, then attach under the caller, then commit". The system-context `attachFile` skips the parent-attachment gate and stamps no requester (measured: `owner_id`, `uploaded_by` and `created_by` all null). So the seat answers Q3 by the ruling: the attach runs as the caller, the parent-attachment gate fires for the caller, and both rows are attributed to the requester. Its check joins the refusal chain's files step, before any mint or launch. Accepting READ as the bar with system attribution would relax a ruled gate, and that is the maintainer's to grant, not this seat's. Constraint: ⛔ no `packages/spec` edit. Prefer one writer: a door in `service-storage` that reuses the `file-attachments` writer under the caller's `ExecutionContext`. If that is impossible without changing `IFileAttachmentService`, stop that item and report the minimal contract change; the seat routes it to the spec lane.

**Answered, not blocking:**
- **Q2 (which page prints): A.** Keep the default-record-page rule with its loud `400`. The seat files the objectui card for a named-page print route at ACCEPT.
- **Q4 (`OS_PRINT_CONSOLE_URL` / `consoleUrl`): A.** Explicit composition.
- **Q5 (CJK in CI):** out of this PR. Provisioning Chromium in CI is a `.github/workflows` edit, a governed surface, so it is the maintainer's. The seat raises it in the round report. The pin stays as built: measured in agent containers, skipped with a warning elsewhere.
- **`packages/spec/llms.txt` and `'@objectstack/spec': patch`:** accepted as the gate-forced package count. The seat declares it to the spec seat at ACCEPT.
- **Out of scope:** the `page.print` liveness row still reads `planned` while two consumers read it, and two printing defects belong to objectui card ②. The seat files both at ACCEPT, after dedupe.

**CI at `4aa215ac5c`:** `Validate Package Dependencies` is red in `check:vendor-export-contract-resolve`, because `npm install better-auth@1.7.3` crashes with `edgesOut` in a scratch directory with its own `package.json`. That is not this PR's: the release PR #23481 failed identically at 2026-10-16T01:40Z, and it is #23788 (`domain:devx`, fix PR #23799 in flight). This PR merges `main` once that lands; no re-run is spent on it. The other checks were still running at this read.

**Size:** 2,795 changed lines before the bind and the attach. If the patch round crosses 3,000, the PR body gains `## 维护者速读(草稿)`, as the dispatch says.

## 席位核对 · patch round 1, item 1 · `domain:services` seat 2 · `session_018VqJPGA1NDNSCZsnecsChP` · 2026-10-16T06:22Z

Read against GitHub at head `fb36ebb704` and on the round's own diff, `5cc84cc6cc..fb36ebb704` (12 files, +460/−92), not against the report (`6209378010` on #22269). ⛔ Not an ACCEPT: item 2 of REWORK `6208156693` is still owed.

- **Item 1, archive under the caller: met.**
  - The attach rule's verdict is extracted once as `mayEditAttachmentParent`, and the `beforeInsert` gate calls the same body.
  - `assertMayAttach` asks the two questions the insert would ask: `explain` for the `sys_attachment` create, then the parent-EDIT verdict.
  - `attachFileAs` runs the one write path with the caller's context, so the real insert gates judge the caller again, `uploaded_by` is stamped by the existing hook, and `sys_file.owner_id` is the caller. A system or user-less context is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403.
  - No spec or `IFileAttachmentService` edit. The new exported type `ICallerFileAttachmentService` widens `@objectstack/service-storage` (`minor`, in the changeset), which this PR's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` already declares. The contract review owed before the queue judges it with the rest.
  - The three ablations each went red where they should. The void legs (no rebuild; an esbuild fold the preflight refused) are declared as void.
- **The two reds on `ff291771f0`: fixed.** `check:slot-lookup` (a typed sharing lookup) and the docs-anchor family are green.
- **CI at `fb36ebb704`:** 38 `success`, 5 roster skips, 0 failure. `Validate Package Dependencies` is green on this head.
- **Answers to the report's open questions:**
  - **Q1, the `explain` pre-check: A, keep it.** It puts the object-permission refusal before the mint and the launch, as ordered. It cannot let anything through that the insert would refuse, because the insert asks again under the caller.
  - **Q2, the showcase grant: A, no change here, and no follow-up card.** The print service follows the app's permissions, which is what the tests show. Nobody has asked for a member-prints demo, so this seat files nothing; a measured need goes to the examples' owner.
- **The PR body: this seat edits it once, at ACCEPT.** It appends the `## 维护者速读(草稿)` (the change is 3,289 lines, over 3,000) with the seat's opinion filled in, and replaces the stale "Binding state" and archive paragraphs. One edit, after item 2, so the body describes the head that lands.
- **Next:**
  1. #23813 lands.
  2. The dev merges `origin/main` and runs the real render with a minted session on both placements (item 2). This seat pokes the dev when #23813 merges.
  3. The contract review (declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`).
  4. ACCEPT, then the maintainer's approval to merge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `19f0174a137cbcf5794cd3d0b7adfee605578a59`
Local-runs: none

PR #23811 (card #22269). The review is owed by the face of the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration. What was read:
- the card's body and all 15 of its comments: the rulings `6204149204` and `6059363716`, the split `6205566815`, the claim `6206177900`, the mint review's pointer `6206951646`, and the dev reports `6208035645`, `6209378010`, `6212023512` and `6212686739`;
- the PR's body, its 41 paths and its 3 comments, including the seat's REWORK `6208156693` and its item-1 check `6209463722`;
- the net diff against the merge base `0cfd0c49bd`, which carries the #23813 fix;
- every file the hunks make a claim about, read at that base. Those paths have not changed between the base and the current `origin/main` `0af559e806`.

None of the 41 paths is governed, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. The gate verdicts are the head's 43 check-runs, latest per name:
- 38 `success`;
- 5 `skipped`: Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke and Temporal Conformance. These are full-battery or opt-in jobs that do not run on `pull_request`;
- 0 failures.

The five required contexts are green.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. `@objectstack/service-print`, a new published package: right.**
- **Exports.** The `exports` map has the root entry only. It exports `PrintServicePlugin`, `PRINT_SERVICE` (`'print'`), `PrintServicePluginOptions`, `IPrintService`, `PrintRecordRequest`, `PrintedRecordFile`, `PrintEngineStatus`, `PRINT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PRINT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`, the three env-name constants, `PrintPlacement` and `PrintPlacementOptions`. `PrintService`, the driver and the deps stay internal.
- **What the plugin registers.** One in-process service and nothing else: no route, no action, no metadata key, no `requires` token and no new error code. Every refusal is typed to the standard or the registered catalogue, as OQ2 A, OQ3 A and OQ6 A rule.
- **Name and lifecycle.** The plugin name follows the `com.objectstack.service.*` siblings. `start()` probes the engine and warns once. That is a functional degradation, so `warn` is the right level. Every collaborator is resolved per call, and the missing-service report waits for `kernel:ready`, so no startup verdict is recorded.

**2. The config options and env names: right.**
- `OS_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH`, `OS_PRINT_BROWSER_ENDPOINT` and `OS_PRINT_CONSOLE_URL` are config values in the `OS_{DOMAIN}_{NAME}` shape. The test-only `OS_TEST_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH` is in the `OS_TEST_*` shape.
- A plugin option wins over its variable. Configuring both placements is `misconfigured`.
- The endpoint must be `ws:` or `wss:`, and it is described by scheme and host only. The console URL must be `http:` or `https:`, with no query and no fragment.
- `OS_PRINT_CONSOLE_URL` as a third setting stands on the seat's answer A to Q4.

**3. `playwright-core` as a dependency: right.**
- It is pinned exact at `1.63.0`, on this package alone.
- The version was already resolved in the lockfile, which gains only the new importer. The esbuild re-resolution noted in `6208035645` is no longer in the net diff.
- It is loaded by dynamic import on the first probe or render. `playwright-core` downloads no browser at install.

**4. `service-storage`'s `ICallerFileAttachmentService`: right.**
- **The public surface.** One new public name: a type, exported from the root entry. `mayEditAttachmentParent` is exported from its own module only, which the `exports` map does not address.
- **A system or user-less context is refused.** Both verbs refuse it with `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 (`requireUserContext`, pinned on both verbs).
- **The insert still judges the caller.** `attachFileAs` reads the parent as the caller; a 403 read folds into the same 404 as a missing row. It writes `sys_file.owner_id` as the caller, and runs the `sys_attachment` insert under the caller's own context, unchanged. Pinned: `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` from the real insert gate, `FILES_DISABLED` as the caller, and `uploaded_by` stamped by the existing hook.
- **`attachFile` is unchanged.** A null caller takes every old branch: the system read, no owner stamp, the system unit.
- **The extraction is faithful.** `mayEditAttachmentParent` is the old body verbatim, with the gate's own read of the parent handed in.
- **Can the pre-check admit anything the insert would refuse?** Yes, by construction, and it fails closed.
  - `assertMayAttach` asks two of the insert's questions, not all of them. The first is the CRUD create verdict, through `ISecurityService.explain`, whose contract is that it runs the enforcement path's own resolution. The second is the parent-EDIT verdict, over the caller's full envelope as the gate forwards it.
  - Three things are judged only at the insert: the size limit (which cannot be known before the render), the organization wall, and any other `sys_attachment` insert gate.
  - Each such refusal arrives after the render. The insert refuses it as the caller, the bytes and the pending row are discarded, and the session is revoked. Pinned: a refused archive still revokes, and nothing is left. So nothing the insert refuses is ever admitted.
  - The print service's header line "so a refused archive never costs a render" overstates this. That is wording, not a blocker.

**5. The render's identity: right, with one pin gap.**
- **Context.** The mint gets the request's own `ExecutionContext`, pinned by object identity, as item 1 of the mint review asked (`6206951646`).
- **TTL.** 60 s, under the 120 s ceiling and over the 30 s budget (pinned).
- **Scope.** The user's own full session, with `activeOrganizationId` set to `context.tenantId` (plugin-auth's mint at base), and never renewed on a read. It is not narrowed to read-only, and on the remote placement it leaves the process. Ruling `6204149204` accepted both.
- **Revocation.** Revoke runs in a `finally`:
  - after a success, a failed render and a refused archive (unit pins, run in Test Core);
  - at the wire after a success (the archive pin's real-mint leg answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`);
  - at the wire after a forced failure (the render pin).
- **No system-attributed PDF.** A `file-attachments` slot without the caller verbs makes `status()` `unavailable` and a print 503 (pinned). The caller verbs refuse the system.
- **No credential in a log, a response or a message.**
  - The endpoint is redacted in every log line and every status. This is pinned against the real `playwright-core` with a dead endpoint that carries a token.
  - The engine-failure message passes through `redact` over both the endpoint and the cookie value. The mint's `token` equals `cookie.value`, so both spellings are covered.
  - No log line carries the cookie.
- **Gap (not blocking, owed before landing): the cookie half of that redaction has no pin that can fail.**
  - `print-service.test.ts` "the minted credential appears in no refusal message" fakes an engine error whose text never held the cookie.
  - The driver's `INTERNAL_ERROR` path is exercised by no test, with Chromium or without it.
  - Removing `input.cookie.value` from the secrets list leaves every suite green.
  - The fix runs in Test Core with no browser. `createChromiumDriver(resolved, launcher)` already takes a launcher. Inject one whose `goto` rejects with a message carrying the cookie value, and assert that the 500's message holds `[redacted]` and not the value.

**6. `IFileAttachmentService` and `IAuthService`: unchanged.**
- No `packages/spec/src/**` path is in the diff. Both contracts were read at base, and both are unchanged on the current `origin/main`.
- `principal-session.ts` imports the contract's `IAuthService` and `PrincipalSession` types, and reads the optional member at call time.

**7. New names, and where they are registered: right.**
- **What is new.** The service slot `print`, the package, and three env names.
- **The slot.** It is a non-core slot, like `cluster`, `sms` and `messaging`, so it needs no `CoreServiceName` entry (which would be a spec change). No route is added, so there is no route ledger or closed query set to declare.
- **The registrations a new package owes are all present:**
  - the Changesets `fixed` group;
  - the lockstep counts: 73 in `backward-compatibility.mdx` and in the publish-smoke comment, 72 in `llms.txt` by its own gate;
  - `packages.mdx`;
  - system-context census rows 47d and 47e;
  - the dogfood inputs in `cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `turbo.json`, with `heldBy` for the gitignored bundle entry, which CI never has;
  - `handwritten-docs.json`.
- **Missing.** The three `OS_PRINT_*` names are not in `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`, a page that calls itself the full `OS_*` list. No gate reads that page; it is prose, for the seat.

**8. The refusal order: right, with one wording gap.**
- The order is: the principal, the engine, the page, the record read as the caller, then the files opt-in plus the attach rule, and only then the mint. Each step is pinned with `code` and `status`, and with nothing minted, rendered or archived.
- **The gap.** When the last probe failed, step ② probes again, and that launches or connects a browser before steps ③ to ⑤ run. No session and no page are involved.
- The PR body, the changeset and the docs say "before any session is minted or browser started", which is not exact on that path. Either narrow the words, or move the re-probe after step ⑤. Not blocking.

**9. Notes on the code for the seat, none of them blocking:**
- **The render budget.** The 30 s budget bounds the open, `goto` and the ready wait. `newContext`, `addCookies`, `newPage`, the fonts wait and `page.pdf` are unbounded, so a stalled remote browser can hold a call past the budget. The credential still ends at its 60 s TTL on the server.
- **A rejecting `revoke()`.** In the `finally`, its error replaces the call's outcome. After a success, the PDF is committed but the caller sees the revoke's error.
- **The organization input.** `attachFileAs` takes `input.organizationId` independently of `context.tenantId`. The print service passes `tenantId`, so the two agree here. The doc of `organizationOfParent` still says "as the system".
- **Stale TSDoc.** Two TSDoc references name `FileAttachmentService.mayAttach`; the verb is `assertMayAttach`.
- **Credential hygiene.** A `ws://` endpoint off loopback carries the minted cookie to the remote browser in cleartext CDP frames. A `consoleUrl` with userinfo is not refused, and it is logged at `info`. Both are worth a line in the docs.

**10. The showcase and the tests: right.**
- **The showcase.** `showcase_invoice` gains `enable: { files: true }` and a default record page that declares `print`. That page therefore also becomes every showcase user's invoice record view. en and zh-CN translations are added.
- **The dogfood source imports.** The dogfood tests import `service-print` source by relative path, which follows the precedent of the route-ledger parity test, and they declare it as an input.
- **The render pin's last change.** It respells the bundle path as its `index.html` entry plus `dirname`, which reads as equivalent.
- **The console pin.** `.objectui-sha` is `daeb77fc84dd` at the green run, at this head, and on the current `origin/main`.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/service-print`: `minor`, right.** A new published package widens the surface. It is in the fixed group, so under pre mode it ships as the group's next `18.0.0-next.N`. The precedent is `service-mailbox`: a new package at `minor` plus the fixed-group edit, with no `pre.json` edit.
- **`@objectstack/service-storage`: `minor`, right.** One new exported type and two new verbs on the registered instance, with `attachFile` unchanged.
- **`@objectstack/spec`: `patch`, right.** `llms.txt` is in spec's `files`, so the count text ships. No schema and no contract changes.
- **The private packages touched** (`example-showcase` and `dogfood`) need no entry.
- **The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line** is on its own line in the PR body (line 3) and in the changeset.
  - It is a widening, at `minor` or above.
  - Nothing is narrowed: `attachFile`, `IFileAttachmentService` and `IAuthService` are unchanged.
  - So no breaking marker and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Escalated to the maintainer, not judged.** Both items are `.github/workflows` edits, a governed surface.
- **E1. CI provisioning of Chromium and a built Console for the render pin.** Two facts for that decision:
  - The dogfood job builds no Console; the Console Pin Gate job does.
  - Both Chromium-gated files look for their browser in `OS_TEST_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH`, then in `$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH/chromium`. That second path is this agent image's own symlink, not a path that `playwright install` creates, and no workflow sets either variable. A CI step must export `OS_TEST_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH`, or the files keep skipping.
- **E2. Installing CJK fonts in CI.** Ruling `6204149204` owes the CJK pin "on each placement CI can reach". Today CI reaches neither placement.

**What the render pin's CI skip leaves unmeasured.** These claims are measured in CI neither on the PR nor in main's full battery:
- a real Chromium render on either placement (`chromium-driver.test.ts` skips too);
- the page binding against the real console;
- the console booting under a minted session through a browser (the #23813 class);
- revoke at the wire after a failed print;
- the cookie's absence from a real failure's message;
- A4 from `@page`, the CJK glyph pin, `TIMEOUT` / 504, and the remote placement's context cleanup.

They are measured only in the dev's container: green 6/6 at `9252cd175e`. Only the path spelling has changed since.

**What carries CI on its own:**
- **Test Core, on this head:**
  - the unit pins of the refusal chain, the TTL and the revoke;
  - the plugin's loudness, against the real `playwright-core`;
  - the config's redaction;
  - service-storage's seven caller-face pins, against a real ObjectQL engine and its insert gates.
- **The archive pin and its wire-level real-mint leg** (9 tests).
  - They need neither Chromium nor a Console, so they carry CI on their own.
  - They run only in main's full battery, because dogfood is skipped on `pull_request` and `merge_group`.
  - On this head they are measured only by the dev's local run (`6212686739`: 9 passed, 6 skipped).

**Dev report `6208035645`.**
- **Q1, the minted session does not boot the console.** Answered by the REWORK `6208156693`. Sub-issue #23813 is closed and its fix is the merge base. Closed.
- **Q2, which page prints.** The seat's answer A holds in code: a 400 for any page that is not the default record page. The objectui card for a named-page route is the seat's to file at ACCEPT.
- **Q3, attribution.** The seat answered "attach as the caller", per OQ7 A. Implemented as ①4 describes. Closed.
- **Q4, `consoleUrl`.** The seat's answer A holds.
- **Q5, CJK in CI.** See E2.
- **Deviations:**
  - **`llms.txt`:** right; see ②.
  - **The gate-required registry touches:** right, as ①7 judges them. The cli tests that cite the inputs script are owned by CI, and Test Core is green on this head. The job logs cannot be reached from here, so whether that package was in this head's affected set is not read.
  - **The lockfile's esbuild drift:** gone from the net diff.
